land.text: Bonoman, defeated in 1723 by Opoku Ware I; the royal line re-established at Takyiman (Techiman) by 1740 paid annual tribute to Asante

successors.note: The Ashanti dossier (af-04-a) dates the gain 1722; the Bono State page has the invasion in 1722-1723 and the defeat in 1723.

capitals.name: Bono Manso
capitals.note: 'it was the capital of the Bono state from the 11th century to 1723'; destroyed in 1723 by Opoku Ware I; Techiman succeeded it after 1723.

correction.text: Bono Manso and its hinterland, 'the earliest of the Akan states', capital from the 11th century

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 'Established: 11th-13th century'; the Bono Manso page dates the town's founding to c. 1000 CE and has Bonoman developed by the 14th and 15th centuries. A 40 km circle round the Bono Manso coordinates (7.70 N, 1.85 W) stands for the early state; no area figure on either page.

correction.text: Bonoman after its expansion, 'expanded Bonoman during the second half of the 15th century'; the Brong country of the modern Brong-Ahafo Region

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox puts the expansion in the 14th-16th centuries, the body text in the second half of the 15th; the page names neighbours (Gonja, Banda, Bonduku, Yendi, Mampong, Offinso, Kete-Krakye) but gives no extent or area. The old Brong Ahafo Region (about 39,000 km2) is a stand-in for the Brong country and is likely too wide in the north; the 17th-century decline is undated in land.

ledger.note: c. 1100: Bono Manso is the capital of the Bono state. Infobox 'Established: 11th-13th century'; 'Bono Manso was settled by the 13th century' and 'was the capital of the Bono state from the 11th century' (Bono Manso page: founded c. 1000 CE). The page treats a founding date of 1295 as unsupported.

region.text: the Brong country round the core, as far as the neighbouring states of Gonja, Banda and Bonduku

ledger.note: second half of the 15th century: Bonoman expands over the Brong country. 'expanded Bonoman during the second half of the 15th century' (infobox: 'Territorial expansion under Ameyaw and Obunumankoma: 14th-16th centuries'). Begho, the northern caravan entrepot from about 1100, lay in the zone.
1722: Asante invades Bono. 'Asante invaded Bono in 1722-1723.' Internal unrest and dynastic conflict had set in from the late 17th century.
1723: Bono is defeated. 'Bono was defeated in 1723, ending its independence.'

1723: Bono Manso is destroyed and Bonoman passes to Asante. 'Bono-Manso was destroyed in 1723 by Opoku Ware I of the Asante Empire'; Techiman succeeded it, a rump 'vassal of the Asante until the late 19th century'. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): source set to the Bono Manso page, which carries the quoted sentences; the Bono State page has 'Bono was defeated in 1723, ending its independence'.
1723: Bonoman ends. The royal line was re-established at Takyiman by 1740 and 'was required to pay annual tribute to Asante'; Ameyaw Kwakye I (d. 1723) was the last independent Bonohene (infobox).

wars.name: Asante conquest of Bono
wars.outcome: Asante victory: Bono defeated in 1723 and Bono Manso destroyed by Opoku Ware I; the Bono royal line later re-established at Techiman as an Asante tributary.
wars.note: The Ashanti dossier dates the gain 1722; the Bono State page has the invasion 1722-1723 and the defeat 1723.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the Brong country, drawn from the modern region as a stand-in.

sources.title: Bono State
sources.note: Infobox dates (established 11th-13th century, expansion 14th-16th, Asante conquest 1723), expansion in the second half of the 15th century, decline in the 17th, Asante invasion 1722-1723, Takyiman by 1740; no area, no capital coordinates.

sources.title: Bono Manso
sources.note: Coordinates 7.70111 N, 1.84611 W; founded c. 1000 CE; capital from the 11th century to 1723; destroyed 1723; Techiman succeeded it.

notes: Bono has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened. No area figure on either; the shapes are a 40 km circle at Bono Manso (coordinates from the Bono Manso page) and the old Brong Ahafo Region as a stand-in for the Brong country. Start year 1100 is a bridge across the infobox range 11th-13th century (confidence 1); the Bono State page says the 1295 date claimed by Meyerowitz is unsupported. Disagreements: the expansion (infobox 14th-16th centuries vs body second half of the 15th); the Ashanti dossier's 1722 gain vs the 1723 defeat here; Takyiman is called Techiman on the Bono Manso page. Not placed: Begho (a punitive Mali expedition in the mid-16th century is on the page), Bono refugees moving to Gyaman, Gonja, Banda and Bonduku as neighbours; Asante's 1740s warfare in Banda, Bouna, Nkoranza and Gonja. The rump at Techiman 1723-late 19th century is a vassal of Asante, not a state of this dossier. Counterpart without dossier: none new (ashanti-empire exists).
